Third conditional: If I had known….explain_en: We use the third conditional to imagine a different past — things that did not happen — and their imaginary results: “If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.”
Third conditional: If I had known….explain_ar: بنستخدم الشرط التالت عشان نتخيل ماضي مختلف (حاجات ما حصلتش) ونتيجتها الخيالية: “If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.”
Third conditional: If I had known….board: past that didn’t happen → imaginary past result

examples.en: If you had told me, I would have helped.
We would have won if we had played better.
examples.ar: كنا كسبنا لو كنا لعبنا أحسن.

check.question: Which sentence talks about an imaginary past?
options: If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I studied, I would pass.
check.why_ar: had studied … would have passed = ماضي ما حصلش.

Third conditional: If I had known….explain_en: Use if + past perfect (had + past participle), then would have + past participle.
Third conditional: If I had known….explain_ar: if + ماضي تام (had + تصريف تالت)، وبعدين would have + تصريف تالت.
Third conditional: If I had known….board: If + had done, … would have done

examples.en: If she had seen the sign, she would have stopped.
examples.ar: لو كانت شافت الإشارة كانت وقفت.

examples.en: I would have called you if I had had your number.
examples.ar: كنت كلمتك لو كان معايا رقمك.

check.question: If they ___ the bus, they wouldn’t have been late.
check.why_ar: بعد if في الشرط التالت: had + caught.

Third conditional: If I had known….explain_en: We often use it to talk about regrets: “If I hadn’t eaten so much, I wouldn’t have felt sick.” Short forms are common in speech: I’d have, she wouldn’t have.
Third conditional: If I had known….explain_ar: بنستخدمه كتير للندم: “If I hadn’t eaten so much, I wouldn’t have felt sick.” وفي الكلام بنختصر: I’d have.
Third conditional: If I had known….board: If I hadn’t …, I wouldn’t have …

examples.en: If I hadn’t missed the alarm, I’d have arrived on time.
examples.ar: لو ما كانش المنبه فاتني كنت وصلت في معادي.

examples.en: He wouldn’t have failed if he’d revised.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: If I would have known, I would have come.
If I had known, I would have come.
If I knew, I would have came.
check.why_ar: ماينفعش would بعد if، والصح had known.

Third conditional: If I had known….explain_en: Instead of would have, use “could have” for possibility or ability and “might have” for something less certain: “If we had taken a taxi, we might have arrived sooner.”
Third conditional: If I had known….explain_ar: بدل would have ممكن could have (كان ممكن/كان هيقدر) أو might have (يمكن كان): “… we might have arrived sooner.”
Third conditional: If I had known….board: could have / might have + past participle

examples.en: If you had asked, I could have lent you money.
examples.ar: لو كنت طلبت كنت قدرت أسلفك.

examples.en: If it hadn’t rained, the match might have been better.
examples.ar: لو ما كانتش مطرت يمكن الماتش كان أحسن.

check.question: If I had trained harder, I ___ the race.
check.why_ar: نتيجة ممكنة في ماضي خيالي → could have won.

Third conditional: If I had known….recap_en: Use if + had + past participle with would, could or might have + past participle to imagine a different past, often to express regret.

Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_en: We use the past perfect to show that one past action happened before another past action: “When I arrived, the film had started.”
Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_ar: بنستخدم الماضي التام عشان نوضح إن حاجة حصلت قبل حاجة تانية في الماضي: “When I arrived, the film had started.”
Past perfect: I had already eaten.board: earlier past → had done · later past → did

examples.en: When we got to the station, the train had left.
examples.ar: لما وصلنا المحطة كان القطر مشي.

examples.en: She was tired because she had worked all day.
examples.ar: كانت تعبانة لأنها اشتغلت طول اليوم.

check.question: Which action happened first? “When I got home, my family had eaten.”
check.why_ar: had eaten هو اللي حصل الأول.

Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_en: Make it with “had” (for everyone) + the past participle: had gone, had seen, had finished.
Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_ar: had مع كل الضماير + التصريف التالت: had gone وhad seen وhad finished.

examples.en: I had never seen the sea before that trip.
examples.ar: عمري ما كنت شفت البحر قبل الرحلة دي.

examples.en: They had already eaten when we arrived.

check.question: By 9 pm, she ___ her homework.
check.why_ar: حاجة خلصت قبل وقت في الماضي → had finished.

Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_en: Compare: “When I arrived, the meeting started” (I arrived, then it started) and “When I arrived, the meeting had started” (it started before I arrived).
Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_ar: قارن: “the meeting started” = الاجتماع بدأ بعد ما وصلت. و“the meeting had started” = كان بدأ قبل ما أوصل.

examples.en: When the police came, the thief had escaped.
examples.ar: لما البوليس جه كان الحرامي هرب.

examples.en: After I had finished, I went out.

check.question: “When I opened the fridge, the milk ___ bad.” (It was already bad.)
check.why_ar: كان باظ قبل ما أفتح → had gone.

Past perfect: I had already eaten.step_title: Stories with already, just, by the time
Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_en: The past perfect makes stories clearer with words like already, just, never, before and by the time: “By the time the guests arrived, we had cooked everything.”
Past perfect: I had already eaten.explain_ar: الماضي التام بيوضح الحكايات مع already وjust وnever وby the time: “By the time the guests arrived, we had cooked everything.”
Past perfect: I had already eaten.board: by the time + past simple, … had done

examples.en: I had just sat down when the phone rang.
examples.ar: لسه كنت قاعد لما التليفون رن.

examples.en: By the time I woke up, everyone had left.

check.question: By the time we arrived, the shop ___.
check.why_ar: المحل قفل قبل وصولنا → had already closed.

Past perfect: I had already eaten.recap_en: Use had + past participle for the earlier of two past actions. It makes the order of events clear, especially with already, just and by the time.

I wish / If only.explain_en: Use “I wish” + past simple for things you want to be different now: “I wish I had a bigger room.” (But I don’t.)
I wish / If only.explain_ar: I wish + ماضي بسيط لحاجات نفسك تبقى مختلفة دلوقتي: “I wish I had a bigger room.” (بس معنديش).

examples.en: I wish I lived near the beach.
I wish I were taller.

check.question: “I don’t speak Chinese.” → “I wish I ___ Chinese.”
check.why_ar: أمنية عن الحاضر → ماضي بسيط spoke.

I wish / If only.explain_en: Use “I wish” + past perfect for regrets about the past: “I wish I had studied harder.” (But I didn’t.)
I wish / If only.explain_ar: I wish + ماضي تام للندم على الماضي: “I wish I had studied harder.” (بس ما ذاكرتش).
I wish / If only.board: I wish + had done = ياريتني كنت

examples.en: I wish I hadn’t said that.
She wishes she had gone to the party.

check.question: “I didn’t bring my umbrella.” → “I wish I ___ my umbrella.”
check.why_ar: ندم على الماضي → had brought.

I wish / If only.explain_en: Use “wish + would” to complain about someone else’s annoying behaviour or to want a change: “I wish you would stop talking!” Not for yourself: “I wish I would…” is wrong.
I wish / If only.explain_ar: wish + would للشكوى من تصرف حد تاني أو لما عايزه يتغير: “I wish you would stop talking!” ومش بنقول “I wish I would”.
I wish / If only.board: I wish you / he / it would …

examples.en: I wish it would stop raining.
I wish my brother would tidy his room.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I wish I would be rich.
check.why_ar: لنفسك في الحاضر → were، مش would.

I wish / If only.explain_en: “If only” is a stronger, more emotional way to say “I wish”: “If only I had more time!” “If only I hadn’t lost my phone!”
I wish / If only.explain_ar: If only طريقة أقوى وأكتر إحساس من I wish: “If only I had more time!”

examples.en: If only I knew the answer!
If only we had left earlier!

check.question: “If only I ___ to her before she left.” (I didn’t.)
check.why_ar: ندم على الماضي → had spoken.

I wish / If only.recap_en: Use wish or if only + past simple for wishes about now, + past perfect for regrets about the past, and + would to want someone else to change.

however / although / despite.explain_en: These words show a contrast between two ideas: “It was cold. However, we went swimming.” They help your speaking and writing sound connected and clear.
however / although / despite.explain_ar: الكلمات دي بتوضح تناقض بين فكرتين: “It was cold. However, we went swimming.” وبتخلي كلامك وكتابتك مترابطة.

examples.en: The test was hard. However, I passed.
examples.ar: الامتحان كان صعب، ومع ذلك نجحت.

examples.en: Although it was late, we kept working.
examples.ar: رغم إن الوقت كان متأخر كملنا شغل.

check.question: Which word shows contrast?
check.why_ar: however بتبين تناقض (ومع ذلك).

however / although / despite.explain_en: “Although” (or “even though”) is followed by a full sentence with a subject and verb: “Although it rained, the match continued.”
however / although / despite.explain_ar: although أو even though بييجي بعدها جملة كاملة فيها فاعل وفعل: “Although it rained, the match continued.”

examples.en: Although he is rich, he lives simply.
I enjoyed the film even though it was long.
examples.ar: الفيلم عجبني رغم إنه كان طويل.

check.question: ___ she was tired, she finished the report.
check.why_ar: بعدها جملة كاملة (she was tired) → Although.

however / although / despite.explain_en: “Despite” and “in spite of” are followed by a noun or -ing, not a full sentence: “Despite the rain…”, “Despite feeling ill, she came.”
however / although / despite.explain_ar: despite وin spite of بييجي بعدهم اسم أو ing، مش جملة كاملة: “Despite the rain” و“Despite feeling ill”.

examples.en: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
In spite of losing, they smiled.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: Despite it was cold, we went out.
Despite the cold, we went out.
Despite of the cold, we went out.
check.why_ar: despite + اسم (the cold)، ومن غير of.

however / although / despite.explain_en: “However” usually starts a new sentence and is followed by a comma: “The hotel was expensive. However, it was very clean.” Don’t join two sentences with just a comma and however.
however / although / despite.explain_ar: however غالباً بتبدأ جملة جديدة وبعدها فاصلة: “… expensive. However, it was very clean.”

examples.en: I wanted to go. However, I was too busy.
examples.ar: كنت عايز أروح، لكن كنت مشغول جداً.

examples.en: The plan is good. However, it is expensive.

check.question: Best punctuation:
options: It was cheap, however it broke.
It was cheap. However, it broke.
It was cheap however, it broke.
check.why_ar: however في أول جملة جديدة وبعدها فاصلة.

however / although / despite.recap_en: Use although + a sentence, despite + a noun or -ing, and however at the start of a new sentence with a comma to show contrast.

must have / can’t have.explain_en: We use must have, can’t have and might have to make guesses (deductions) about the past based on evidence: “The streets are wet. It must have rained.”
must have / can’t have.explain_ar: بنستخدم must have وcan’t have وmight have عشان نستنتج حاجة حصلت في الماضي من دليل: “The streets are wet. It must have rained.”

examples.en: She’s smiling — she must have passed.
He can’t have seen us; he didn’t wave.

check.question: “The ground is wet.” Best guess:
check.why_ar: استنتاج عن الماضي → must have + rained.

must have / can’t have.explain_en: “Must have + past participle” means you are almost sure something happened: “You must have been tired after the trip.”
must have / can’t have.explain_ar: must have + تصريف تالت = متأكد تقريباً إنها حصلت: “You must have been tired after the trip.”

examples.en: They must have left already — the lights are off.
You must have worked hard.

check.question: “Sara got 100%.” — “She ___ very hard.”
check.why_ar: متأكدين إنها ذاكرت → must have studied.

must have / can’t have.explain_en: “Can’t have” (or couldn’t have) means you are almost sure something did NOT happen. Don’t use “mustn’t have” for this meaning.
must have / can’t have.explain_ar: can’t have أو couldn’t have = متأكد إنها ما حصلتش. وماينفعش mustn’t have بالمعنى ده.
must have / can’t have.board: can’t have done = مستحيل يكون حصل

examples.en: He can’t have finished already — he started five minutes ago.
examples.ar: مستحيل يكون خلص — لسه بادئ من خمس دقايق.

examples.en: She couldn’t have known about the party.

check.question: “I saw Ali in Cairo at 5.” — “He ___ been in Riyadh then.”
check.why_ar: مستحيل يكون في الرياض → can’t have.

must have / can’t have.explain_en: Use might have, may have or could have when you think something possibly happened: “I can’t find my keys. I might have left them at work.”
must have / can’t have.explain_ar: might have أو may have أو could have لما تكون الحاجة ممكن حصلت: “I might have left them at work.”
must have / can’t have.board: might / may / could have done = يمكن حصل

examples.en: She’s late. She might have missed the bus.
They could have gone to the cinema.

check.question: “Where’s Omar?” — “I’m not sure. He ___ gone home.”
check.why_ar: مش متأكد → might have.

must have / can’t have.recap_en: Use must have for things you are almost sure happened, can’t have for things that almost certainly didn’t, and might or could have for possibilities.

make or do?.explain_en: Arabic often uses one verb (عمل) for both “make” and “do”, so learners mix them up. In English, the noun decides which verb we use.
make or do?.explain_ar: بالعربي بنستخدم “عمل” للاتنين، فبنلخبط بين make وdo. في الإنجليزي الاسم اللي بعدهم هو اللي بيحدد.
make or do?.board: make or do? → it depends on the noun

examples.en: I need to do my homework.
Let’s make a cake!

check.question: Choose the correct phrase:
check.why_ar: مع homework بنقول do.

make or do?.explain_en: Use “do” for tasks, jobs and general activities: do homework, do the dishes, do exercise, do a job, do your best, do business.
make or do?.explain_ar: do للمهام والشغل والأنشطة العامة: do homework وdo the dishes وdo exercise وdo your best.
make or do?.board: do + homework / the dishes / exercise / your best

examples.en: I do exercise three times a week.
examples.ar: بعمل رياضة تلات مرات في الأسبوع.

examples.en: Just do your best!

check.question: Can you ___ the shopping today?
check.why_ar: التسوق مهمة → do the shopping.

make or do?.explain_en: Use “make” when you create or produce something: make a cake, make a mistake, make a noise, make a decision, make a plan, make friends, make money.
make or do?.explain_ar: make لما بتصنع أو تنتج حاجة: make a cake وmake a mistake وmake a decision وmake friends وmake money.
make or do?.board: make + a mistake / a decision / money / friends / noise

examples.en: Don’t worry, everyone makes mistakes.
We need to make a decision now.

check.question: Please don’t ___ so much noise.
check.why_ar: مع noise بنقول make.

make or do?.explain_en: The best way is to learn them as fixed pairs (collocations). Notice: make a phone call, make an effort, make progress — but do a favour, do research, do well.
make or do?.explain_ar: أحسن طريقة إنك تحفظهم كأزواج ثابتة: make a phone call وmake progress، لكن do a favour وdo research وdo well.
make or do?.board: make progress · do research · do me a favour

examples.en: You’ve made great progress!
Could you do me a favour?

check.question: Which pair is correct?
check.why_ar: الصح make a mistake وdo a favour.

make or do?.recap_en: Use do for tasks and activities and make for creating or producing things — and learn common pairs like make a mistake and do homework by heart.
